# The Deep Rift

Most warlocks make pacts. They bargain with fiends, pledge to archfey, seek out great old ones in the darkness between stars. Warlocks of the Deep Rift never chose their patron. Something inside the Rift chose them.

It doesn't speak. It doesn't bargain. It doesn't even seem to want anything — or if it does, it hasn't bothered to explain. One day, you could hear the Rift humming at a frequency only you could perceive. And then you could do things. Reach through the Veil. Distort probability. Feed the Rift by killing, and receive its scraps in return.

The horror isn't what it wants from you. The horror is that you don't know — and your power keeps growing anyway.

## Expanded Spell List

The Deep Rift lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

| Spell Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 1st | Dissonant Whispers, Tasha's Hideous Laughter |
| 2nd | Misty Step, Blindness/Deafness |
| 3rd | Clairvoyance, Fear |
| 4th | Dimension Door, Phantasmal Killer |
| 5th | Scrying, Telekinesis |

## Rift-Touched

*1st-level Deep Rift feature*

When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, the Rift claims a piece of it — and you get what's left. You gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum 1). The Rift feeds. You receive the scraps. You've stopped asking whether that should bother you.

## Veilwalker's Luck

*6th-level Deep Rift feature*

The Rift has learned to nudge probability on your behalf — whether you asked or not. When you make an ability check or saving throw, you can add 1d10 to the roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before the outcome is determined.

Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

## Rift Resilience

*10th-level Deep Rift feature*

The Rift hardens what it touches. When you finish a short or long rest, choose one damage type. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one. The Rift adapts to what hurt you last — and protects its investment.

## Hurl Through the Rift

*14th-level Deep Rift feature*

Once per long rest, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can hurl them through the Veil. The target vanishes, yanked through the space between realities. At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it left — or the nearest unoccupied space — and takes 10d10 psychic damage from what it saw while it was gone.

The target doesn't remember the experience clearly. It remembers enough.
